title: Purged yet residual weakness; sin no longer reigns but leftovers remain
source_text: XXI. Illi ergo quos Deus per Christum in gratiam recepit a peccatorum quidem maculis purgati sunt, verum non ita ut nihil sordium in iis supersit. Anima quidem eorum Christo medente curata convalescit; vis morbi in iis fracta est, & sunt extra mortis periculum; sed tamen semper est aliquid ex languore & infirmitate priori residuum. Denique peccatum in iis regnum amplius non obtinet, & vires ejus quotidie magis ac magis atteruntur; sed tamen haerent adhuc quaedam illius reliquiae, quibuscum est ipsis assidue pugnandum.
pass_a_gloss: Those therefore whom God has received into grace through Christ are indeed purged from the stains of sins, yet not so that nothing filthy remains in them. Their soul, healed by Christ the physician, convalesces; the force of the disease in them is broken, and they are out of danger of death; yet there is always something residual from prior languor and infirmity. Finally sin no longer obtains a kingdom in them, and its powers are worn down more and more daily; yet certain remains of it still cling, with which they must continually fight.
pass_b_english: Grace purges stain and breaks disease-force—out of death's danger—yet residual languor remains.
Sin no longer reigns; its strength wears down daily, but leftovers demand continual fight.
